Not fully. Your June 2025 finding was accurate for what it covered (2021–2024), but it has been superseded.

The current evidence (version 2, as of 2026-11-12) extends the period through 2025. It flags a tree-cover loss candidate of 13.5 ha in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha property. The JRC 2020 forest map agrees with the event at 0.98, but the assessment is still pending corroboration because 2025 is the latest year in the series and a later year is needed to confirm it.

This evidence does not establish:
- whether the loss is persistent
- whether it is deforestation or land-use change, since Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation
- the cause
- whether it was legal
- any compliance status

So I would not describe the file as "no loss detected" beyond 2024. Update it to show a 2025 loss candidate pending corroboration.
